name: Banking Regulation Act, 1949
change: Established a regulatory framework for banks in India and strengthened the role of the Reserve Bank of India in supervising banking operations.
impact: Improved stability and control over the banking system, reducing risks of bank failures.

name: Bank Nationalisation Policy, 1969
change: Major private banks were nationalized to expand credit access to agriculture, small industries, and rural areas.
impact: Improved financial inclusion and rural banking access but led to inefficiencies and rising non-performing assets.

name: Bank Nationalisation Expansion, 1980
change: Additional banks were brought under government control to strengthen public sector dominance in banking.
impact: Expanded reach of banking services but increased government control reduced operational efficiency.

name: Narasimham Committee Reforms, 1991
change: Introduced structural reforms including deregulation, private bank entry, capital adequacy norms, and NPA recognition.
impact: Improved efficiency, competition, and transparency in the banking sector.

name: Narasimham Committee II, 1998
change: Focused on bank consolidation, stronger capital norms, and improved governance structures.
impact: Strengthened financial stability and prepared banks for global competition.

name: SARFAESI Act, 2002
change: Allowed banks to recover non-performing assets without court intervention through asset seizure.
impact: Improved recovery of bad loans and reduced banking sector stress.

name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, 2014
change: Mass opening of bank accounts for unbanked populations with direct benefit transfer integration.
impact: Expanded banking access and enabled digital financial inclusion.

name: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
change: Introduced time-bound insolvency resolution process for companies and individuals.
impact: Improved credit discipline and strengthened banking sector health.

name: Public Sector Bank Merger Policy, 2019
change: Merged multiple public sector banks to create larger, stronger banking institutions.
impact: Improved efficiency, capital strength, and global competitiveness of Indian banks.

name: Digital Banking and UPI Expansion Policy, 2020
change: Expansion of digital payment systems like UPI and mobile banking platforms across India.
impact: Revolutionized payments and financial access, making India a global leader in digital banking.
